title: Context Across Asynchronous Operations knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which approach best supports reliable work with Context Across Asynchronous Operations?
options: Store credentials and production secrets directly in the source file.
Use await with try/catch, run independent tasks concurrently with bounded concurrency, and make cancellation/retries explicit.
Skip input validation because Node.js applications run on a trusted server.
Assume every supported runtime has identical APIs and scheduling behavior.
questions.answer_key: Use await with try/catch, run independent tasks concurrently with bounded concurrency, and make cancellation/retries explicit.
questions.explanation: Use await with try/catch, run independent tasks concurrently with bounded concurrency, and make cancellation/retries explicit. The example and verification steps should make this practice observable.

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed under Context Across Asynchronous Operations?
questions.explanation: “Request context” is one of the subtopics retained from the supplied Node.js curriculum for this lesson.

questions.prompt: Before relying on a Context Across Asynchronous Operations implementation, what verification is most useful?
options: Assume the API behaves as expected without running a check.
Ignore failures so the program continues silently.
Use the same code regardless of documented version differences.
Verify the documented result in a supported runtime and test one failure or boundary case.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result in a supported runtime and test one failure or boundary case.
questions.explanation: A small deterministic check plus a failure/boundary case helps distinguish a correct design from a happy-path-only example.
